title: Why you can't catch the space station by speeding up
one_idea: Speeding up in orbit raises your altitude, making you move slower; spacecraft catch the station by orbiting ahead and waiting.
audience_misconception: Viewers believe a spacecraft should simply accelerate to catch up with the station, as if driving faster on a road.

analogy.source_term: Spacecraft catch the station by going to a slightly higher orbit ahead of it, not by accelerating toward it.
mapping: higher orbit ahead of the station
car A pulling ahead on the outer lane
the station in the lower orbit behind
car B on the inner lane, going faster but covering less distance per lap
orbit phasing — higher orbit = longer path = slower lap time
outer lane takes longer to complete a lap than the inner lane
analogy.limitation: Unlike cars on a road, spacecraft cannot simply brake to wait — they use thrusters to raise or lower their orbit precisely.

claims.claim: SpaceX Crew-13 docked with the International Space Station in under 8 hours using orbital phasing.
In orbital mechanics, forward thrust raises the orbit's altitude rather than directly increasing speed relative to the target.
Orbit phasing involves adjusting orbital altitude so a spacecraft in a higher orbit is overtaken by a target in a lower orbit.

sources.claim: SpaceX Crew-13 docked with the ISS in under 8 hours

mechanism.step: Fire engines forward to raise the orbit to just ahead of the station
At the higher orbit, orbital period is longer, so the spacecraft falls behind the station
The station in its lower, faster orbit catches up to the spacecraft from behind
Spacecraft and station meet in the same orbit; docking proceeds

concepts.name: Orbit phasing
concepts.definition: Adjusting your orbital altitude to change your lap speed so a target catches up to you from behind.

concepts.name: Orbital period
concepts.definition: The time it takes to complete one full orbit; higher orbits have longer periods.

A spacecraft firing its engines should catch the space station, right? Wrong. In orbit, speeding up raises your altitude, which makes you slower. Here is how spacecraft actually catch the station — and how Crew-13 did it in under 8 hours.
